items.title: Coral-associated denitrification is seasonally variable and species-specific
items.author: Christian Wild
items.content: We explore the influence of seasonal environmental change and the trophic strategy of the coral host on the denitrification activity of four Red Sea corals. We show that denitrification rates are generally higher in the spring/summer compared to the autumn/winter and show the highest rates in the fully heterotrophic coral Dendrophylliidae indet.

items.title: Unexpected functional role of the transactivation domain for nuclear import of STAT5
items.author: Gerhard Müller-Newen
items.content: Nuclear import of the transcription factor STAT5 depends on a short motif in the transactivation domain revealing a distinct trafficking mechanism and a potential therapeutic target in STAT5-driven disease.

items.title: Targeting chondroitin synthase 1 attenuates hyperplastic arterial remodeling via gene therapy
items.author: Cho Yeow Koh
items.content: This study investigates the role of chondroitin synthase 1 in hyperplastic arterial remodeling associated with chondroitin sulfate over-synthesis. Reducing chondroitin synthase 1 via RNA interference regulates multiple cellular processes and pathways, restores vascular compliance and elasticity, and preserves cardiovascular function.

items.title: Physics informed machine learning predicts binding free energy changes in protein-RNA complexes upon mutations
items.author: Yunhui Peng
items.content: Pred-MutPRI is a machine learning method that predicts how mutations affect protein-RNA binding affinity. By combining thermodynamics, structural features, sequence information, and AlphaFold3-derived strain measures, it outperforms existing predictors and achieves strong accuracy on independent test sets (PCC = 0.705).

items.title: A multi-co-chaperone pre-secretion assembly directs type VI secretion system toxin delivery
items.author: Yue-zhong Li
items.content: We investigate how a distantly encoded Myxococcus xanthus toxin is prepared for type VI secretion. A multichaperone presecretion assembly links the toxin to a PIPY protein that recruits it to the secretion spike.
